content: Public bodies in the UK spent £3.4 billion on private consultants in the last year, marking a £1.3 billion increase compared to the pre-pandemic period. The rise in spending on consultants, which escalated during the Covid pandemic, has not returned to earlier levels. This situation presents a significant challenge for Keir Starmer's government, which aims to reduce consultant spending by 50% during its term. Recent reports indicate that KPMG has secured a major government contract for civil servant training as part of this trend. Academic Prem Sikka criticized the reliance on consultants, arguing they provide little value in complex organizational settings. Is there anything else I can help with?
